newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY-NZ-Fitzy courageous, but ACC not impressed.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY-NZ-Fitzy courageous, but ACC not impressed.

text.p: MELBOURNE, July 28 - Sean Fitzpatrick believes his troublesome knee won't cripple his chances of playing the home Tri-Series rugby tests against South Africa and Australia in the next three weeks, NZPA reports.

Though the puffed joint had to be punctured and drained before last night's 33-18 win over the Wallabies at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, he said surgery would be eventually required to remove some damaged cartilage.
But "Captain Courageous" may not be too popular with the ACC, which has been campaigning vigorously against players' returning to action before complete recovery from injuries.
Both codes of rugby claimed the biggest chunk of ACC's payout last year.
ACC's Wellington-based spokesman Alan Seay said he believed Fitzpatrick was receiving the best medical advice on tour.
"He shouldn't be playing if there's a danger of aggravating the injury," Seay said.
He said the All Blacks were seen by young sports people as role models.
Nevertheless, Fitzpatrick's sportsmanship, determination, and competitive edge were best illustrated over the last week.
He aggravated an old knee injury when he copped a heavy tackle on the side of his thigh in the 35-32 win over South Africa a week ago.
A specialist who examined the injury in Melbourne on Tuesday, gave the 34-year-old no chance of making his record 89th test appearance.
The injury kept Fitzpatrick from running all week until Thursday night when he surprised his coach John Hart and all others by completing a two-hour training session here.
It is what makes Fitzpatrick so good a player and leader.
His competitiveness nullifies some of the disadvantages he faces on the field, Hart said.
"He never ceases to amaze me," the All Black coach remarked.
"On Wednesday I gave him absolutely no chance of playing. He trained the next day."
Against the Springboks it was the only second time in his entire test career that he had to leave the field because of injury.
On Saturday night the battered, bloodied and bruised skipper never thought of abandoning his ship.

Blood poured from his mouth after a scrum engagement was mistimed and his Wallaby counterpart John Eales rained punches on him twice -- the second time completely unprovoked when Fitzpatrick was on the ground holding a Wallaby players' boot.
Eales left play and ran five metres to unleash another flurry of punches to Fitzpatrick's face and head.
The All Black captain, not one to retaliate, merely pointed out the incident to English referee Ed Morrison who was assisted by a touch judge in clarifying what happened.
Eales was lucky to remain on the field, and let off without a warning. Carlos Spencer converted the subsequent penalty.
Fitzpatrick said he would see Auckland specialist Barry Tietjens about his knee when he returned home.
"There are just bits of cartilage in there that needs cleaning up. That's why it swells," he said.
"We've got a rest this week so that'll help."
